subject: MAP: ACME close playbook + performance results and variant recommendation
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Hudson <kate.hudson@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + perf test plan (ACME)

Kate, thanks again for the time today — attaching an updated MAP (v3) with milestones toward contract signature. The key open item we promised to validate during your PoC window is runtime performance at target concurrency and the perceived quality delta between the 13B quantized variant and the heavier 70B FP16 family.

High-level perf test plan (what we'll run in the next 48–72h):
- Workloads: mix of short auth prompts (<= 32 tokens), medium transaction summaries (32–120 tokens), and long policy-generation prompts (120–600 tokens).
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency for generation, TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput (tokens/sec), end-to-end throughput (requests/sec at target concurrency), and model output quality (BLEU-like heuristics + small human eval for 100 anchors).
- Concurrency targets: baseline 20 concurrent sessions, stretch up to 80 concurrent sessions (ACME target).
- Model variants to test: rw-v1-13b-q8 (quantized), rw-v1-13b-int8 (alternate quant), rw-v1-70b-fp16 (high-quality baseline).
- Acceptance threshold (prelim): p95 latency <= 250ms for short prompts; TTFT < 120ms; sustain >= 80 concurrent sessions with <5% error rate. Final thresholds based on your go/no-go note below.

Deliverables: perf_summary_20260518.pdf (key numbers + recommendation), raw run artifacts, and the updated MAP spreadsheet (acme_map_v3.xlsx) with dates for canary and production rollouts.

Please confirm the acceptance thresholds and the decision deadline you want us to aim for — we put May 24 as close target in the MAP.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Kate Hudson <kate.hudson@acmepayments.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmepayments.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP draft + perf test plan (ACME)

Thanks, Vanessa — that plan looks good. A couple clarifications from our side before you run everything: 

1) Tight latency targets for short prompts are important to our UX team: ideally p95 <= 150ms for prompts under 32 tokens, p50 should be sub-50ms.
2) TTFT targets: <80ms for first byte whenever possible.
3) Concurrency: we need to demonstrate solid behavior at sustained 80 concurrent sessions (we have a planned peak at that level during holiday flows).
4) Quality: if the 13B quant shows visible regressions on the 100 anchor set vs 70B FP16, we'll need a plan that either prefers 70B in production or uses a hybrid routing policy (13B for low-latency flows, 70B for high-fidelity flows).

Decision timeline: Can we plan for a go/no-go by May 21 EOD? If you need extra runway, May 24 is acceptable but we'd prefer the earlier date. Also request: include a cost delta estimate (incremental cost/month at our projected 20M tokens/month).

Kate Hudson
Head of Product, AI Platforms | Acme Payments
kate.hudson@acmepayments.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Hudson <kate.hudson@acmepayments.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP draft + perf test plan (ACME) — initial runs attached

Team / Kate — I pushed the initial perf runs to our staging harness and attached a short summary (perf_summary_20260518.pdf) plus raw artifacts. Notes up front: tests run on a single-region Dedicated cluster (g4dn-like instance mix) to mirror ACME's planned region. This is not final hardware parity but is representative for latency/throughput comparisons.

Key numbers (median of three runs each, mixed prompt set):
- rw-v1-13b-q8
  - p50 latency (short prompts): 32ms
  - p95 latency (short prompts): 140ms
  - TTFT: 58ms
  - sustained throughput (tokens/sec, single node): 9,200 toks/s
  - max concurrent sessions before queueing rose >5%: 85
  - CPU/GPU utilization: 72%/68%
  - Qualitative quality delta vs 70B: small on anchors (avg rating 4.3/5 vs 4.6/5)

- rw-v1-13b-int8
  - p50: 28ms
  - p95: 165ms
  - TTFT: 62ms
  - throughput: 10,400 toks/s
  - max concurrency: 90 (but higher p95 tail)
  - note: slightly more variation in p95; quant stability ops item

- rw-v1-70b-fp16
  - p50: 85ms
  - p95: 230ms
  - TTFT: 110ms
  - throughput: 18,100 toks/s
  - max concurrency: 160 (expected, more memory headroom when batching)
  - quality: highest on anchor set (avg rating 4.6/5)

Cost/ops note: 13B variants are ~0.28x cost of 70B FP16 per token in our Dedicated pricing model. The quality delta on the 100-anchor set is measurable but small; we recommend a focused human review for the 12 anchors where the 13B variant dropped below acceptability.

Attachments: perf_summary_20260518.pdf, perf_run_artifacts_20260516.tar.gz

I'll follow up with per-prompt-class breakdowns if you want — right now the short-prompt behavior is excellent for rw-v1-13b-q8 and meets Kate's p95 target.

—Marcus Lin
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + perf test plan (ACME) — recommendation

Quick recommendation to the deal team: given ACME's latency emphasis and the small measured quality delta, we should position rw-v1-13b-q8 as the default production model for conversational/short flows. Proposed rollout:
- Canary (48h): route 10% of production traffic to rw-v1-13b-q8, with canary monitoring for the 12 identified anchors and production NPS/latency signals.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to rw-v1-70b-fp16 for requests flagged by the quality classifier (we can use a quick similarity threshold on embeddings to route high-fidelity cases).
- Cost/volume estimate: at projected 20M tokens/month, expected spend delta vs 70B = -72% (approx). Provide precise cost delta in the MAP.

Notes: need SE ops to validate that caching and prefix-KV behavior is identical between variants; also confirm cold-start behavior for TTFT under our selected Dedicated configuration. Marcus, can you validate those two items in the next run?

Tessa Morgan
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Kate Hudson <kate.hudson@acmepayments.com>

Subject: Re: MAP draft + perf test plan (ACME) — quick Qs

Thanks team — the initial numbers are encouraging. Two asks before we lock timelines: 
1) Can you give us a delta cost table (13B-q8 vs 70B-fp16) for our 20M tokens/month profile (incl. estimated Dedicated commit cost)?
2) We want a short A/B canary (48h) that specifically measures business KPIs: auth success latency (ms), fraud-model pipeline latency impact, and a small manual QA review of the 12 anchors.

If those are green, we'll be ready to sign. I'll route the DocuSign internally once you send the final MAP and the cost table.

Kate

Subject: FINAL: ACME MAP + perf appendix — recommendation and close path

Kate / Liam — attaching the final MAP (acme_map_v3.xlsx) and perf appendix (perf_summary_20260518.pdf). Summary & recommended close path below: 

Executive summary:
- Recommendation: Default production model = rw-v1-13b-q8 for latency-sensitive conversational flows; rw-v1-70b-fp16 available for high-fidelity flows and fallback.
- Rationale: 13B-q8 meets ACME's p95 target for short prompts (140ms measured) and TTFT (58ms). It sustains the requested 80-concurrency requirement in our Dedicated staging runs. Cost is materially lower (~28–30% of 70B per token).

Planned MAP milestones (dates):
- 2026-05-20: Final MAP and cost delta shared (this email + attachments).
- 2026-05-21: SE ops runs cold-start verification & KV cache parity check (Marcus).
- 2026-05-22 to 2026-05-24: 48h production canary (10% traffic) running A/B for the three business KPIs Kate requested.
- 2026-05-24 EOD: Target contract signature (DocuSign link below).

Canary acceptance criteria (pass = proceed to full prod):
- auth success latency: p95 improvement or parity within 15% vs baseline
- fraud-pipeline downstream latency: <10% degradation in p95
- manual QA: no more than 3 of the 12 anchors rated below acceptable quality (pre-agreed manual rubric)

Fallbacks and operational knobs:
- Auto-fallback to rw-v1-70b-fp16 for flagged high-fidelity requests.
- Escalation: SRE on-call will open an incident if p95 latency exceeds 300ms for 5 consecutive minutes.

Cost delta (high level for 20M toks/mo):
- rw-v1-13b-q8: ~$9,200/mo
- rw-v1-70b-fp16: ~$32,000/mo
- Estimated savings: ~$22,800/mo (~71% reduction)

Next steps for signature: please confirm May 24 target or request May 21 for earlier close. We will upload a DocuSign envelope for the final commitment once you confirm.

Thanks — pushing the attachments and the HubSpot deal update now.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
